# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21

### Added

- **XP & enchanting**: the game gains its first progression currency and a way to spend it, all on **zero new assets** (a procedural XP bar + effect-coloured table sprite, synthesized blip/shimmer). The save schema bumps **v6 → v7** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
  - **XP** (`state.xp`, banked points; `XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level): earned from **mob kills** (hostiles more than passives, the **boss a jackpot**; babies give none, like drops — table in `mobXp.ts`), **mining ores** (scaled by rarity), and **fishing** catches. A green **XP bar** above the hotbar fills toward the next level with the level number over it. Unlike status effects, XP is a long-term currency and is **not cleared on death**
=== save-format headings ===
1:# Save format & compatibility
3:## Schema
5:`SaveData` (version 7) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
21:Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
23:Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
33:### Version history
35:- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
36:- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
37:- **v5** (unchanged for fishing) — the active cast is the session-only `state.fishing` field (a transient bobber, like in-flight arrows and thrown spears); it is never serialized and is cleared on respawn. The fishing rod and raw/cooked fish are additive items saved by string id, and a catch is an ordinary inventory change. No worldgen change, so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
38:- **v5** (unchanged for the living world — saplings, bone meal & grass spread) — every effect is an ordinary block edit that rides the `changes` diff: a planted sapling, a grown tree's wood and leaves, and re-grassed dirt all persist with no new fields, and bone meal is an additive item saved by string id. The `Sapling` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 50) so existing saved block ids never shift. Crucially, the runtime tree grower (`systems/treeGrowth.ts`) shares **no** code with worldgen's hash-pinned `placeTrees`, so the generated terrain is byte-identical and **neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved**.
39:- **v5** (unchanged for villagers & trading) — the villager mob is transient like every mob, and trading needs no persisted state: a trade is a station-gated recipe (`station: "villager"`) run through the existing `craft` command, the open trade station (`craftingStation`) is session-only, and there are no per-trade use caps to store. **Emerald** and any traded goods save by string id in the existing inventory slots. No worldgen change (villagers spawn into the passive population; there are no village structures), so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved.
40:- **v5** (unchanged for creepers & TNT) — the creeper mob, gunpowder, and the explosion system add no persisted state: mobs are transient, **a creeper's lit fuse and a primed TNT block's countdown are session-only** (`MobState.fuseTimer` and `state.primedTnt` are never serialized — like the boss and in-flight arrows). Gunpowder and the TNT item save by string id; a **placed TNT block persists in the block diff** like any block, and a save written mid-fuse reloads with that TNT as an inert, un-lit block (and no creeper). There is no worldgen change — creepers are spawned and TNT is crafted — so neither the `version` nor `WORLDGEN_VERSION` moved. Blast-destroyed blocks are ordinary block-diff edits.
41:- **v5** (unchanged for cow/pig & coal) — the cow and pig mobs (and their meat/leather drops) add no persisted state; mobs are transient and the new foods save by string id. Coal ore, coal, and charcoal are likewise additive (the ore persists in the block diff, the items by string id), so the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the new coal worldgen changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` is bumped `7` → `8`**: a world whose recorded version differs discards its stale block-diffs and reboots from its seed. Coal runs on its own PRNG (`placeCoal`), so only underground coal cells differ from a v7 world — the surface, existing ores, trees, and structures are byte-identical (the meshing and structural-probe tests stay green; only the byte hashes were re-rolled).
42:- **v5** (unchanged for caves & lighting) — the lighting system adds no persisted state (light is a derived cache, recomputed at load), and lava is worldgen, not a saved field. So the save _schema_ stays at version 5. But the deep-cave lava changes the deterministic terrain baseline, so **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped `minecraft_save_v6` → `minecraft_save_v7`**: old block-diffs were computed against the lava-free world and must never be applied to the new one. Pre-lava saves are discarded in practice. Torches are additive items/blocks, persisted by string id / in the block diff like any other placed block.
43:- **v5** (unchanged for ranged combat & the endgame boss) — bows, arrows, the Cursed Totem, the Dragon Heart, and the Dragon Sword are **additive items**, persisted by string id in the existing inventory/container slots, so no schema change was needed. **Arrows in flight, the boss, its minions, and the `victory` flag are all transient** (never serialized — like mobs), and there is no worldgen change (the boss is summoned, not generated), so neither the `version` nor `SAVE_KEY` moved.
44:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7.
45:- **v4** — adds optional `blockEntities` (chest contents). `migrateSaveV3toV4` is a pure version bump (absent → restores as no containers), so **`SAVE_KEY` was unchanged** at the time (player-placed chests only; worldgen and the index formula were untouched) and v1/v2/v3 saves load fine.
46:- **v3** — adds optional `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger`, and `spawnPoint`. `migrateSaveV2toV3` is a pure version bump (the new fields stay absent and restore as engine defaults), so **`SAVE_KEY` is unchanged** and v1/v2 saves load fine.
49:- Unknown future versions are rejected (treated as no save).
51:## Profiles & worlds
53:Saves are organized two levels deep — a **profile** owns a list of **worlds**, and each world holds one `SaveData` blob — across three localStorage keys. All three are versioned `{ version: 1, ... }` envelopes and their readers are **total** (malformed entries are dropped, never thrown):
59:`worldgenVersion` records the `WORLDGEN_VERSION` (`lib/game/config.ts`, currently 8) the world was generated under. This **replaces the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump**: when the worldgen baseline changes, bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, and a world whose recorded version differs has its stale block-diffs discarded and reboots from its stored seed — per-world, with no key rename and without touching unaffected worlds.
65:### Legacy migration
67:`migrateLegacySave` (`lib/game/legacyMigration.ts`) runs once on first boot, gated on the **absence** of `minecraft_profiles_v1` (its presence is the already-migrated flag, which survives a rollback that re-creates the legacy key). When a legacy `minecraft_save_v7` exists it creates a default "Player" profile (carrying the old global skin) and **copies** the save into one "My World" blob, then removes the legacy key — the copy precedes the delete so a mid-migration failure can never lose the original. A brand-new player with **no** legacy save gets nothing here; the menu opens straight into the create-profile form (`ProfileSelect` renders it whenever there are zero profiles), so their first act is naming and skinning a profile.

=== README 21-34 ===
## Controls

- `W A S D`: Move · `Space`: Jump · `C`: Crouch
- `W + CapsLock`: Sprint (drains hunger)
- `Mouse`: Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)
- `Left click` (hold): Break block / attack mobs
- `Right click` or `E`: Place/interact, or throw a selected spear
- `1..9`: Select hotbar slot
- `I`: Inventory & crafting · `F`: Eat food · `Shift+U`: Emergency unstuck
- `V`: Camera view (first-person → third-person rear → third-person front)
- `Esc`: Pause menu (save / load / reset, **Save & Quit to Worlds**, sound/music volume sliders, and the Appearance skin picker live there) · `F3`: Debug overlay

New here? The [player manual](docs/manual.md) walks through your first day, survival, crafting, farming, mobs, and more.

=== manual 54-76 ===
## Controls

| Key / input        | Action                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `W` `A` `S` `D`    | Move (walk / strafe)                                                |
| `Space`            | Jump                                                                |
| `C`                | Crouch (slower, careful movement)                                   |
| `W` + `CapsLock`   | Sprint — faster, but drains hunger                                  |
| Mouse              | Look around (double-click the game first to lock the pointer)       |
| Left-click (hold)  | Break the targeted block / attack a mob                             |
| Right-click or `E` | Place/interact, or throw a selected spear                           |
| `1`–`9`            | Select a hotbar slot                                                |
| `I`                | Open / close inventory & crafting                                   |
| `F`                | Eat the selected food, or drink a selected potion                   |
| `V`                | Cycle camera: first-person → third-person rear → third-person front |
| `Shift` + `U`      | Emergency unstuck (teleport to safe ground if wedged)               |
| `Esc`              | Pause menu (save / load / reset, volume sliders, skin picker)       |
| `F3`               | Debug overlay (FPS, position, daylight, mob counts)                 |

Gameplay is always **eye-relative**: even in third person, your reach, aim, and
audio follow where your eyes point, and the crosshair stays centered.

## Survival
=== reference 11-24 ===
## World types

Chosen when you create a world (alongside the name and seed) and fixed for its
life. All four share the same five biomes — they reshape terrain, not the biome
mix. Source: `lib/world/worldTypes.ts` + `terrainConfigFor` in `lib/world/generation.ts`.

| Type      | Terrain                                                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Default   | Balanced terrain with every biome — the original generator                                  |
| Superflat | Level ground at a fixed height; a builder's canvas (caves and ores still generate below)    |
| Amplified | Exaggerated relief — towering peaks and deep valleys                                        |
| Islands   | A raised sea breaks the land into scattered, gently sloped islands with deep ocean channels |

## Recipes
=== tuning 15-27 ===
## Player feel — physics & movement

`GRAVITY`, `JUMP_VELOCITY`, `WALK_SPEED`, `SPRINT_SPEED`, `CROUCH_SPEED`,
`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.

Read by `systems/playerMotion.ts`. These set the moment-to-moment feel.
`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.

## Survival pressure — the main difficulty dial

```
1	# Save format & compatibility
2	
3	## Schema
4	
5	`SaveData` (version 7) in `lib/game/types.ts`:
6	
7	- world `seed`
8	- `worldType` (optional) — the generation preset (`"default"` | `"flat"` | `"amplified"` | `"islands"`); absent ⇒ `"default"`. Like `seed`, it is fixed for the world's life and the world must always regenerate with it, since the block-diffs were recorded against that terrain
9	- a block **diff** list — `changes: [blockIndex, blockId][]`; edits that revert to the generated baseline are pruned (player-placed crops, beds, furnaces, chests, and both halves/states of doors ride this list — they are ordinary block edits)
10	- inventory slots with durability **and enchantments** (36 slots; the first 9 are the hotbar). Each `SavedSlot` is `{ id, count, durability?, enchantments? }`; `enchantments` (`{ id, level }[]`) ride durable gear only and are validated on load (`restoreSlot` — known ids via `Object.hasOwn`, levels clamped to `1..ENCHANT_MAX_LEVEL`). The same path serializes chest contents
11	- `xp` (optional) — banked experience points (`XP_PER_LEVEL` points = one level). Earned from kills/ore/fishing, spent at the enchanting table. Restored by `restoreXp` (finite, ≥ 0). Unlike effects, XP is a currency and is **kept across death**
12	- equipped armor
13	- selected hotbar slot (0–8)
14	- player position — validated on load by `restorePlayerPosition` (`lib/game/save.ts`): coords keep their fractional part (the player isn't grid-aligned) but a missing or non-finite (NaN/Infinity) position is rejected, leaving the fresh spawn in place so a corrupt blob can't load a broken world or slip past the `position.y < 2` unstuck net
15	- `dayClock`, `hearts`, `hunger` (all optional) — time of day and player stats, so sleeping through the night and a hurt/hungry player survive a reload
16	- `spawnPoint` (optional, `{x,y,z}` or null) — the bed respawn point; respawn falls back to a random land point when it is null or the block there is no longer a bed
17	- `blockEntities` (optional) — chest contents as `{ index, slots }[]`, keyed by the block's voxel index (the same index space as `changes`). Only **non-empty** chests are stored; an empty one carries no data and is recreated empty when opened. On load each entry is kept only if that index still holds a Chest block. This is the first per-block metadata in the format — `lib/game/save.ts` (`serializeContainers` / `readContainers`) handles it
18	- `effects` (optional) — active status effects as `{ id, remaining }[]` (remaining in seconds). Drink-granted buffs (Speed/Strength/Regeneration/Fire Resistance/Water Breathing) and the rotten-flesh Poison hazard live in `state.effects` (a Map) and persist here, but are **cleared on death**, so a saved-then-reloaded world resumes whatever was active at save time. On load, `restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) drops unknown ids and non-positive/garbage durations
19	- `lootedChests` (optional) — voxel indices of dungeon loot chests the player has already opened or broken. Dungeon chests are placed by worldgen, so their contents are **not** in `changes`/`blockEntities` until accessed; the engine fills them lazily on first access (loot seeded from `world.seed ^ index`) and records the index here. Because an emptied chest drops out of `blockEntities`, this set — not the chest's emptiness — is what prevents a re-roll on reload. The session-only set of _which_ indices are dungeon chests/spawners is not stored; it is re-derived from the seed each load via `collectDungeonSites` (`lib/world/generation.ts`). Handled by `serializeLootedChests` / `readLootedChests` in `lib/game/save.ts`
20	
21	Each world's `SaveData` is stored in its own localStorage key, `minecraft_world_save_<worldId>` (`worldSaveKey` in `lib/game/worlds.ts`). Read/write and restore validation live in `lib/game/save.ts` — `readSave`/`writeSave` take the key as a parameter and the `Storage` is injectable for tests; `GameEngine.serialize()` produces the save from live state, and `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts` maintains the block diff. (The legacy single-world key `SAVE_KEY` = `minecraft_save_v7` is now read only once, by the migration described under [Profiles & worlds](#profiles--worlds).)
22	
23	Audio volume preferences live under a **separate**, global key (`minecraft_audio_v1`, `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`), shared across all profiles and not part of any world save or its versioning.
24	
25	**Per-voxel light is never serialized.** It is a derived cache (`world.light`), recomputed from the blocks at load by `computeFullLight` and patched locally on every edit (`lib/world/lighting.ts`); the bake reads only `world.blocks`, so the save needs no lighting field.
26	
27	Continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and the oxygen/drowning meter all live only
28	in transient `GameTimers`/state. Saving, reloading, or respawning resets them
29	(breath restores to full). The status-effect **accumulators** (`effectRegenTimer`,
30	`effectPoisonTimer`) are likewise transient — but the effects **themselves**
31	(`state.effects`) persist via the `effects` field above and survive a reload.
32	
33	### Version history
34	
35	- **v7** (XP & enchanting) — adds optional top-level `xp` and an optional `enchantments` array on each `SavedSlot`. `migrateSaveV6toV7` is a pure version bump (absent → xp 0, no enchantments). XP persists and is **kept across death** (it's a currency, not a status effect); enchantments ride the existing `inventorySlotsSnapshot`/`restoreSlot` path (shared by inventory and chests) and are validated on load. The **Enchanting Table** item saves by string id and the `EnchantingTable` `BlockId` is **appended** (id 52) so saved block ids never shift. No worldgen change — **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8**.
36	- **v6** (status effects, brewing & potions) — adds optional `effects` (`{ id, remaining }[]`). `migrateSaveV5toV6` is a pure version bump (absent → no active effects), so pre-effect saves load clean. Effects persist but are cleared on death; `serializeEffects`/`restoreEffects` (`lib/game/save.ts`) round-trip and validate them. Potions, glass bottles, and the **Brewing Stand** item save by string id; the `BrewingStand` `BlockId` is **appended at the end** of the enum (id 51) so existing saved block ids never shift, and a placed stand persists in the block diff like any block. No worldgen change — the new effects/recipes touch no generation — so **`WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays at 8** and the determinism hashes are untouched.
```

46:- **v5** — adds optional `lootedChests` (opened/broken dungeon loot chests). `migrateSaveV4toV5` is a pure version bump (absent → no dungeon chests yet looted). Unlike v3/v4, **`SAVE_KEY` is bumped to `minecraft_save_v6`** here — not because of the save _shape_ (the field is additive) but because the dungeon worldgen changed the deterministic terrain baseline, so old block-diffs would index against the wrong world. Pre-dungeon saves are therefore discarded in practice; the migration keeps the version chain complete regardless. `readSave` chains v1 → v2 → v3 → v4 → v5 → v6 → v7.

The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**\n  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide\n  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact\n  - **Spectator**: a free camera — fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, with no interaction at all; hostiles ignore you entirely and the HUD/hotbar hide\n  - **Switching** modes mid-game (pause menu) refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, sets flight to match the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator — so it's always safe to flip between them\n  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than comparing the raw id — so the four modes share one set of seams (the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, the block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`). `gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` + a v8 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV7toV8`); unlike `worldType` it's the _current_, switchable value, and the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. New `setGameMode`/`toggleFlight`/`creativeGiveItem` commands; new `FLY_SPEED`/`FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` tunables\n\n## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21"
}

31	## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)
32	
33	- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command)`, advances `step(dt, input)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`) and the world size is overridable for fast headless tests.
34	- `state.ts` — `GameState` (player with `yaw`/`pitch`, inventory, mobs and thrown
35	  spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, mining
36	  progress, timers) plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
37	- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
38	- `blockChanges.ts` — the delta tracker behind the save format: tracked block writes against the worldgen baseline; reverted edits drop out of the save.
39	- `systems/` — one module per mechanic, each a function over `GameState`:
40	
41	### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)
42	
43	0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
44	1. Stuck detection / auto-unstuck (`STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`)
45	2. Death check + respawn countdown (while dead, only mobs tick)
46	3. Sleep gate: while `state.sleepTimer > 0`, `step` decrements the fade and returns (full freeze, like pause); at zero it skips the clock to the next morning
47	4. Player movement & physics (`systems/playerMotion.ts` — derives direction from `yaw`, scratch vectors, no per-frame allocations)
48	5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
49	6. Mining progress and block breaking (`systems/mining.ts`; placement also lives here)
50	7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula); immediately after, `systems/weather.ts` sets the **transient** `state.weather` (rain/snow/clear) as a pure function of `dayClock` + seed — cosmetic only: never serialized, never touches spawn/daylight balance
51	8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
52	9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
53	10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
54	11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
55	12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
56	13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)
57	
58	**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.
59	
60	**Endgame boss & victory.** A `"boss"` `MobKind` is summoned from a held Cursed Totem via a step in the `placeBlock` precedence (`GameEngine.trySummonBoss`, which seeds placement and refuses if a boss already exists). Defeating it (`removeMobAt`) drops a Dragon Heart, sets the session-only `state.victory`, and emits `bossDefeated`. Boss HP, player-relative bearing, horizontal block distance, and the victory flag reach React through `GameSnapshot.boss`/`victory`; the `boss` object is rebuilt only when one of its rounded visible values changes, avoiding sub-block React churn. Renderer-side hostile health bars are procedural `THREE.Sprite`s attached to each mob model and updated directly from `MobState.hp`, so ordinary mob damage does not enter the React snapshot. A new `"boss"` kind requires entries in all five exhaustive `Record<MobKind>` tables (`MOB_TEMPLATES`, `MOB_DROPS`, `CALL_INTERVALS`, `MOB_AMBIENT_SOUNDS`, `MOB_ATTACK_SOUNDS`).

test("the pause menu freezes the game and resumes it", async ({ gamePage: page }) => {
  await calmDaytime(page);
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape"); // unlocked, so Escape pauses directly
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Back to Game" })).toBeVisible();

  const clock1 = await page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.dayClock);
  await page.waitForTimeout(250);
  const clock2 = await page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.dayClock);
  expect(clock2).toBe(clock1);

  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Back to Game" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Back to Game" })).not.toBeVisible();
  await page.waitForTimeout(250);
  expect(await page.evaluate(() => window.__monecraft!.engine.state.dayClock)).toBeGreaterThan(clock2);
});

test("picking a skin persists across a reload", async ({ gamePage: page }) => {
  await calmDaytime(page);
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape"); // unlocked, so Escape pauses directly
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Robot skin" }).click();

  // The skin now lives on the active profile, not a global key.
  const storedSkin = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const manifest = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("minecraft_profiles_v1")!);
    return manifest.profiles.find((p: { id: string }) => p.id === manifest.activeProfileId).skinId as string;
  });
  expect(storedSkin).toBe("robot");

  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__monecraft !== undefined, undefined, { timeout: 30000 });
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Robot skin" })).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "true");
  await expect(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Steve skin" })).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "false");
});

## Game modes — done on `feat/game-modes`

All four Minecraft modes (Survival · Creative · Adventure · Spectator), built in 8 focused, individually-green commits:

| Commit | What landed |
|---|---|
| `feat(modes): add GameMode plumbing & save v8` | `gameModes.ts` (enum + predicates), `WorldMeta`, save v7→v8 migration, engine field + snapshot |
| `feat(modes): creative mode` | invulnerable / no-hunger / instant free-build / flight (double-tap Space) |
| `feat(modes): creative inventory palette` | all-items searchable palette, click-to-give |
| `feat(modes): spectator mode` | noclip, unseen, no-interaction, mobs ignore you |
| `feat(modes): adventure mode` | survival minus block editing (tests; gate was shared) |
| `feat(modes): switch mode in the pause menu & pick at creation` | `setGameMode` + reset, pause selector, creation picker, world badge |
| `docs(modes): document game modes` | manual, reference, save-format, tuning, architecture, testing, README, CHANGELOG |
| `fix(modes): keep the taller pause menu on-screen; e2e save v8` | e2e-gate fixes |

The design uses **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `mobsThreaten`, …) so all four modes share one set of seams rather than scattered `mode === "x"` checks.

Pick a mode when you create a world (next to world type and seed) and switch it any time from the pause menu. Zero new assets; save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with no worldgen change.\n\n## Modes\n\n| Mode | Damage / hunger | Break / place | Flight | Interact | Mobs | Inventory |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Survival | yes | yes | no | yes | hostile | normal |\n| Creative | no | instant, free | yes | yes | ignore you | all-items palette |\n| Adventure | yes | **no** | no | yes | hostile | normal |\n| Spectator | no | no | yes (noclip) | **no** | ignore you | hidden |\n\n- **Creative** — fly (double-tap `Space`, then `Space`/`C` to rise/descend), invulnerable, no hunger, instant break of any block, place without consuming. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item**.\n- **Adventure** — survival in every way except you can't break or place blocks.\n- **Spectator** — a free camera: fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, no interaction; hostiles ignore you and the HUD/hotbar hide.\n- **Switching** mid-game refills bars, clears pending hazard damage, matches flight to the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator.\n\n## Design\n\nA new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than scattering `mode === \"x\"` checks. So the four modes share one set of seams: the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`, HUD in `MinecraftGame.tsx`.\n\n`gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's the **current, switchable** value; the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. `128-149`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Skip chest spills for creative breaks.**
Creative skips normal drops/XP at Line 147, but chests still call `spillChestOnBreak` first. That lets creative breaking transfer chest contents / emit pickup events, or refuse the break when the inventory is full, which breaks the creative no-drop/free-break contract.

     resetMining(state);
     return;
   }
+  if (creative && chestIndex !== null) state.containers.delete(chestIndex);
```

## **Pause Menu Redesign: Styling & Patterns Research**

### **1. Pause-Menu CSS Rules (from `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/app/hud.css`)**

Here are all the pause-menu-related CSS rules quoted in full:

```css
.pause-overlay {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: 9;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  animation: mc-fade-in 140ms ease-out;
}

.pause-menu {
  display: grid;
  gap: 8px;
  width: min(92vw, 320px);
  justify-items: stretch;
  max-height: 100vh;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 6px 0;
}

.pause-title {
  text-align: center;
  color: var(--mc-text-light);
  font-size: 22px;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-shadow: var(--mc-text-shadow);
  margin-bottom: 10px;
}

.mc-button {
  padding: 9px 16px;
  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: 14px;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--mc-text-light);
  text-shadow: var(--mc-text-shadow);
  background: var(--mc-tile-button), var(--mc-button);
  border-style: solid;
  border-width: 2px;
  border-color: #a8a8a8 #2c2c2c #2c2c2c #a8a8a8;
  outline: 2px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85);
  cursor: pointer;
  user-select: none;
  transition: background-color 80ms ease;
}

.mc-button:hover,
.mc-button:focus-visible {
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-color: #c3cbe5 #34394d #34394d #c3cbe5;
}

.mc-button:active {
  border-color: #2c2c2c #a8a8a8 #a8a8a8 #2c2c2c;
  transform: translateY(1px);
}

.mc-button:disabled {
  opacity: 0.55;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

.mc-button.danger {
  background: #8c3a34;
  border-color: #c98179 #4a1713 #4a1713 #c98179;
}

.pause-reset-row {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 8px;
}

.pause-modes {
  margin-bottom: 6px;
}

.pause-modes-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 6px;
  margin-top: 4px;
}

.mode-option[aria-pressed="true"] {
  border-color: #f0be3c;
  outline: 1px solid rgba(240, 190, 60, 0.6);
}

.pause-sound {
  display: grid;
  gap: 8px;
  margin-top: 4px;
}

.pause-sound-row {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 64px 1fr;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 10px;
  color: var(--mc-text-light);
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-shadow: var(--mc-text-shadow);
}

.pause-skins {
  display: grid;
  gap: 6px;
  margin-top: 4px;
}

.pause-skins-title {
  color: var(--mc-text-light);
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-shadow: var(--mc-text-shadow);
}

.pause-skins-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  gap: 6px;
}

.skin-swatch {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 3px;
  padding: 6px 4px;
  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: 11px;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--mc-text-light);
  text-shadow: var(--mc-text-shadow);
  background: var(--mc-tile-button), var(--mc-button);
  border-style: solid;
  border-width: 2px;
  border-color: #a8a8a8 #2c2c2c #2c2c2c #a8a8a8;
  cursor: pointer;
  user-select: none;
}

.skin-swatch:hover,
.skin-swatch:focus-visible {
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-color: #c3cbe5 #34394d #34394d #c3cbe5;
}

.skin-swatch[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-color: #f0be3c;
  outline: 1px solid rgba(240, 190, 60, 0.6);
}

.pause-save-message {
  text-align: center;
  color: #aef79f;
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 700;
  text-shadow: var(--mc-text-shadow);
}

.pause-controls {
  margin-top: 12px;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  background: var(--mc-tile-dirt), rgba(20, 14, 8, 0.9);
  outline: 2px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85);
  display: grid;
  gap: 3px;
}

.pause-controls-row {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 16px;
  color: #d4d4d4;
  font-size: 11px;
  text-shadow: 1px 1px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7);
}

.pause-controls-row span:last-child {
  color: #f4f4f4;
  font-weight: 700;
}

.mc-slider {
  appearance: none;
  width: 100%;
  height: 18px;
  margin: 0;
  background: var(--mc-tile-button), var(--mc-button);
  border-style: solid;
  border-width: 2px;
  border-color: #2c2c2c #a8a8a8 #a8a8a8 #2c2c2c;
  outline: 2px solid rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.85);
  cursor: pointer;
}

.mc-slider:focus-visible {
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-color: #c3cbe5 #34394d #34394d #c3cbe5;
}

.mc-slider::-webkit-slider-thumb {
  appearance: none;
  width: 12px;
  height: 18px;
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-style: solid;
  border-width: 2px;
  border-color: #c3cbe5 #34394d #34394d #c3cbe5;
}

.mc-slider::-moz-range-thumb {
  width: 12px;
  height: 18px;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-style: solid;
  border-width: 2px;
  border-color: #c3cbe5 #34394d #34394d #c3cbe5;
}
```

**Key layout patterns:**
- `.pause-menu` is a **grid** with `gap: 8px`, capped at `320px` width, with `overflow-y: auto` for tall content
- Most sections use nested grids (e.g., `.pause-modes-grid` is `grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr`, `.pause-skins-grid` is `repeat(3, 1fr)`)
- Consistent 6px–10px margins/gaps between sections
- All interactive elements reuse `.mc-button` or variants (`.skin-swatch`, `.mode-option`)

### **2. CSS Variables & Theme (from `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/app/base.css`)**

All `--mc-*` variables defined in `:root`:

```css
:root {
  color-scheme: light;

  /* Minecraft chrome palette: gray panels with light/dark bevel edges. */
  --mc-panel: #c6c6c6;
  --mc-panel-deep: #8b8b8b;
  --mc-bevel-light: #ffffff;
  --mc-bevel-dark: #373737;
  --mc-slot-well: #8b8b8b;
  --mc-text: #404040;
  --mc-text-light: #fcfcfc;
  --mc-text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55);
  --mc-button: #6f6f6f;
  --mc-button-hover: #7f8caf;
  /* Item tooltip: near-black fill with Minecraft's violet gradient border. */
  --mc-tooltip-bg: #100010ee;
  --mc-tooltip-border-a: #28007f;
  --mc-tooltip-border-b: #5b00b5;
  --mc-tooltip-sub: #a8a8a8;
  /* Monospace stack, kept for the F3 debug readout (column alignment). */
  --mc-font-mono: "Lucida Console", Monaco, "Courier New", monospace;
  /* Generated noise tiles (set at runtime by installUiTiles). The chrome grain
     tiles default to `none` so panels fall back to their flat color pre-install
     and during SSR. */
  --mc-tile-dirt: none;
  --mc-tile-stone: none;
  --mc-tile-panel: none;
  --mc-tile-well: none;
  --mc-tile-button: none;
  /* Strength of the always-on screen-edge vignette (fed into rgba alpha). */
  --mc-vignette: 0.28;
}
```

**Used in pause menu:**
- `--mc-text-light` (#fcfcfc) — all text color
- `--mc-text-shadow` (2px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.55)) — drop shadow on all text
- `--mc-button` (#6f6f6f) — base button background (with optional `--mc-tile-button` noise overlay)
- `--mc-button-hover` (#7f8caf) — hover/focus/pressed state
- `--mc-tile-button`, `--mc-tile-dirt` — optional noise textures (default `none`)

For tab styling, you should reuse these variables consistently—especially the button colors and text shadow for any tab-selector element.

### **3. Existing Tab / Segmented Control Patterns**

**Search results:** No `role="tab"`, no `aria-selected`, no `<details>`/`<summary>` elements found in the codebase.

**What DOES exist:** `aria-pressed` toggle pattern used extensively:
- **PauseMenu.tsx**: Game Mode selector and Skin swatches use `aria-pressed={condition}` on buttons
- **CreateWorldForm.tsx**: World type and game mode options use `aria-pressed={condition}`
- **Styling for selection**: `.mode-option[aria-pressed="true"]` and `.skin-swatch[aria-pressed="true"]` both apply gold border + outline (Minecraft classic selection highlight):

```css
.mode-option[aria-pressed="true"] {
  border-color: #f0be3c;
  outline: 1px solid rgba(240, 190, 60, 0.6);
}

.skin-swatch[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background: var(--mc-button-hover);
  border-color: #f0be3c;
  outline: 1px solid rgba(240, 190, 60, 0.6);
}
```

**Recommendation:** For tab redesign, adopt the `aria-pressed` toggle pattern (rather than full `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"`) to stay consistent with the codebase. Pair it with the same gold selection highlight.

No save-format or worldgen impact.\n"

## Approved Plan:
# Pause menu — tabbed layout to cut clutter

## Context

Pressing **Esc** opens the pause menu, but everything is stacked in one long scrolling column: 5 action buttons, a 4-button Game Mode grid, two volume sliders + a mute button, a skin grid, and a 12-row controls reference. It overflows short viewports (we recently had to make it scroll). The fix is to split that mix of **frequent actions / occasional settings / static reference** into **three tabs**, so each view is short and you land on the actions you came for.

**No gameplay/engine/save changes** — this is purely a reorganization of `components/game/PauseMenu.tsx` and its CSS. Reuses the existing `mc-button` + gold `aria-pressed` selection styling; zero new assets.

## Design

```
.pause-overlay > .pause-menu
  "Game Menu" (title)
  [ Back to Game ]            ← pinned: the most common action, always one click away
  [ Game | Options | Controls ]   ← tab bar (aria-pressed buttons)
  .pause-panel                ← only the active tab's content renders
  {saveMessage}               ← pinned at the bottom, visible from any tab
```

Tab contents (current pieces just move into panels, unchanged):

- **Game** (default): Save Game · Load Save · Reset World (with its confirm step) · Save & Quit to Worlds · **Game Mode** selector.
- **Options**: Sound + Music sliders + Mute · **Appearance** (skin grid).
- **Controls**: the `CONTROLS` reference table.

## Implementation

### `components/game/PauseMenu.tsx`
- Add tab state: `type PauseTab = "game" | "options" | "controls"`; `const [tab, setTab] = useState<PauseTab>("game")`.
- Keep `Back to Game` and the title above the tab bar; keep the transient `saveMessage` pinned below the panel (Save/Load/Reset live in the Game tab but the toast should always show).
- Tab bar: three `mc-button pause-tab` buttons with `aria-pressed={tab === id}` + visible text "Game"/"Options"/"Controls" (matches the codebase's `aria-pressed` toggle convention — same pattern as the mode/skin selectors; no new ARIA tablist needed).
- Render **only the active panel** (conditional), so inactive content isn't in the DOM. Move the existing markup verbatim into the panels: the action buttons + `pause-modes` block → Game; `pause-sound` + `pause-skins` → Options; `pause-controls` → Controls.
- `confirmingReset` state and the `volumeSlider` helper stay as-is; props/callbacks are unchanged.

### `app/hud.css` (where the pause styles already live)
- Add `.pause-tabs` (a 3-column grid, `gap: 6px`), `.pause-tab` (a compact `mc-button` — smaller font/padding), and `.pause-tab[aria-pressed="true"]` reusing the gold highlight (`border-color: #f0be3c; outline: 1px solid rgba(240,190,60,0.6)`) like `.mode-option`/`.skin-swatch`.
- Add `.pause-panel { display: grid; gap: 8px; }` so panel children stack like today.
- Keep `.pause-menu`'s `max-height: 100vh; overflow-y: auto` as a safety net (the Controls panel is the tallest). Existing `.pause-modes`/`.pause-sound`/`.pause-skins`/`.pause-controls` rules are reused unchanged.

## Tests — `components/game/PauseMenu.test.tsx`
- The Game tab is the default, so the existing **Back to Game / Save / Load / Reset / Save & Quit / Game Mode** tests pass unchanged, and the pinned **save-message** test is unchanged.
- The four **audio + skin** tests now click the **Options** tab first (`getByRole("button", { name: "Options" })`) before querying the sliders / mute / skins.
- Add one test: **tabs switch the visible section** — default shows "Save Game"; clicking **Options** reveals "Sound volume" and hides "Save Game"; clicking **Controls** shows a known row (e.g. "Inventory").

## Docs
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` → a short **Changed** entry (pause menu reorganized into Game/Options/Controls tabs).
- `docs/manual.md` + `README.md`: the pause-menu one-liners already list save/load/reset/mode/volume/skins — tweak to note they're now under tabs (one phrase each).

## Verification
- Gate: `bun run lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `bun test` (esp. `PauseMenu.test.tsx`), `bun run build`. `bun run test:e2e` — the existing "pause menu freezes" smoke test only clicks the still-pinned **Back to Game**, so it passes unchanged (the React shell/pause UI changed, so run it).
- Manual pass (`Esc` in-game): the menu fits without a long scroll; tabs switch cleanly; **Back to Game** and **Esc** both resume; switching Game Mode (Game tab), volume/skins (Options tab), and the controls list (Controls tab) all work.

## Scope & workflow
Small, single-component UI refactor, but landed via a **branch + PR** so it gets CI + CodeRabbit review:
- Branch `refactor/pause-menu-tabs` off `main`.
- Commit(s) — Conventional Commit subjects, body explaining the why, **no `Co-Authored-By` trailer**. Likely two focused slices: `refactor(ui): pause menu into Game/Options/Controls tabs` (component + CSS + tests) and `docs: note pause-menu tabs` (CHANGELOG + manual/README). Keep `bun run lint` green at each.
- Verify gate green, then open the PR against the fork's `main` (`gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main`), no AI-attribution lines.
- **Pushing / opening the PR are user-authorized** — I won't push until you ask.

No save-format or worldgen impact.

the rest is split across\n * three tabs — Game (save/load/reset/quit + game mode), Options (sound +\n * appearance), and Controls (the key reference) — so no single view is a long\n * scroll.\n */\nexport default function PauseMenu({\n  saveMessage,\n  audioSettings,\n  onAudioSettingsChange,\n  gameMode,\n  onGameModeChange,\n  skinId,\n  onSkinChange,\n  onBack,\n  onSave,\n  onLoad,\n  onReset,\n  onQuitToWorlds\n}: PauseMenuProps) {\n  const [confirmingReset, setConfirmingReset] = useState(false);\n  const [tab, setTab] = useState<PauseTab>(\"game\");\n\n  const volumeSlider = (label: string, value: number, onValue: (volume: number) => void) => (\n    <label className=\"pause-sound-row\">\n      <span>{label}</span>\n      <input\n        className=\"mc-slider\"\n        type=\"range\"\n        min={0}\n        max={100}\n        value={Math.round(value * 100)}\n        onChange={(event) => onValue(Math.max(0, Math.min(1, Number(event.target.value) / 100)))}\n        aria-label={`${label} volume`}\n      />\n    </label>\n  );\n\n  return (\n    <div className=\"pause-overlay\">\n      <div className=\"pause-menu\">\n        <div className=\"pause-title\">Game Menu</div>\n        <button className=\"mc-button\" onClick={onBack}>\n          Back to Game\n        </button>\n\n        <div className=\"pause-tabs\">\n          {TABS.map((entry) => (\n            <button key={entry.id} className=\"mc-button pause-tab\" aria-pressed={tab === entry.id} onClick={() => setTab(entry.id)}>\n              {entry.label}\n            </button>\n          ))}\n        </div>\n\n        <div className=\"pause-panel\">\n          {tab === \"game\" && (\n            <>\n              <button className=\"mc-button\" onClick={onSave}>\n                Save Game\n              </button>\n              <button className=\"mc-button\" onClick={onLoad}>\n                Load Save\n              </button>\n              {confirmingReset ? (\n                <div className=\"pause-reset-row\">\n                  <button className=\"mc-button danger\" onClick={onReset}>\n                    Confirm Reset\n                  </button>\n                  <button className=\"mc-button\" onClick={() => setConfirmingReset(false)}>\n                    Cancel\n                  </button>\n                </div>\n              ) : (\n                <button className=\"mc-button\" onClick={() => setConfirmingReset(true)}>\n                  Reset World\n                </button>\n              )}\n              <button className=\"mc-button\" onClick={onQuitToWorlds}>\n                Save &amp; Quit to Worlds\n              </button>\n              <div className=\"pause-modes\">\n                <div className=\"pause-skins-title\">Game Mode</div>\n                <div className=\"pause-modes-grid\">\n                  {GAME_MODE_PRESETS.map((preset) => (\n                    <button\n                      key={preset.id}\n                      className=\"mc-button mode-option\"\n                      aria-pressed={preset.id === gameMode}\n                      aria-label={`${preset.label} mode`}\n                      onClick={() => onGameModeChange(preset.id)}\n                    >\n                      {preset.label}\n                    </button>\n                  ))}\n                </div>\n              </div>\n            </>\n          )}\n\n          {tab === \"options\" && (\n            <>\n              <div className=\"pause-sound\">\n                {volumeSlider(\"Sound\", audioSettings.master, (volume) => onAudioSettingsChange({ master: volume }))}\n                {volumeSlider(\"Music\", audioSettings.music, (volume) => onAudioSettingsChange({ music: volume }))}\n                <button className=\"mc-button\" aria-pressed={audioSettings.muted} onClick={() => onAudioSettingsChange({ muted: !audioSettings.muted })}>\n                  {audioSettings.muted ? \"Unmute Sound\" : \"Mute Sound\"}\n                </button>\n              </div>\n              <div className=\"pause-skins\">\n                <div className=\"pause-skins-title\">Appearance</div>\n                <div className=\"pause-skins-grid\">\n                  {SKIN_PRESETS.map((preset) => (\n                    <button\n                      key={preset.id}\n                      className=\"skin-swatch\"\n                      aria-pressed={preset.id === skinId}\n                      aria-label={`${preset.label} skin`}\n                      onClick={() => onSkinChange(preset.id)}\n                    >\n                      <PixelImg src={skinPortraitUrl(preset.id)} alt=\"\" size={32} aria-hidden />\n                      <span>{preset.label}</span>\n                    </button>\n                  ))}\n                </div>\n              </div>\n            </>\n          )}\n\n          {tab === \"controls\" && (\n            <div className=\"pause-controls\">\n              {CONTROLS.map(([action, keys]) => (\n                <div key={action} className=\"pause-controls-row\">\n                  <span>{action}</span>\n                  <span>{keys}</span>\n                </div>\n              ))}\n            </div>\n          )}\n        </div>\n\n        {saveMessage && <div className=\"pause-save-message\">{saveMessage}</div>}\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  );\n}\n"
}

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Game modes**: the game gains Minecraft's four ways to play — **Survival** (the original), **Creative**, **Adventure**, and **Spectator** — as a single per-player axis you pick at world creation and can switch any time from the pause menu, all on **zero new assets**. The save schema bumps **v7 → v8** (additive), with **no worldgen change**
10	  - **Creative**: fly (double-tap **Space**, then Space/crouch to rise/descend), take no damage and never hunger, break any block instantly, and place blocks without consuming them. The recipe book is replaced by a searchable **palette of every item** — click one to pull a stack into your inventory. The survival HUD bars hide
11	  - **Adventure**: survival in every respect (damage, hunger, mobs, combat, doors/chests/trading) **except you can't break or place blocks**, so a built world stays intact
12	  - **Spectator**: a free camera — fly through terrain (noclip), invisible and invulnerable, with no interaction at all; hostiles ignore you entirely and the HUD/hotbar hide
13	  - **Switching** modes mid-game (pause menu) refills your bars and clears any pending hazard damage, sets flight to match the mode, and lifts you out of a wall when leaving Spectator — so it's always safe to flip between them
14	  - **Architecture**: a new `lib/game/gameModes.ts` holds the `GameMode` union plus **intent predicates** (`takesDamage`, `canEditBlocks`, `freeBuild`, `canInteract`, `canFly`, `isNoclip`, `usesInventory`, `mobsThreaten`) that each system gates on, rather than comparing the raw id — so the four modes share one set of seams (the damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts`, the block edits in `mining.ts`, aggro in `mobAI.ts`, flight/noclip in `playerMotion.ts`). `gameMode` rides the existing per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` + a v8 `SaveData` field + `migrateSaveV7toV8`); unlike `worldType` it's the _current_, switchable value, and the transient `isFlying` is never serialized. New `setGameMode`/`toggleFlight`/`creativeGiveItem` commands; new `FLY_SPEED`/`FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` tunables
15	
16	## [0.10.0] - 2026-06-21
17	
18	### Added
